AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health and trajectory are genuinely strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered $111.18B revenue (+16.6% YoY), EPS of $2.01 (+21.8% YoY), gross margin expansion to 49.3%, and operating cash flow of $28.70B (+19.8% YoY). The balance sheet has materially improved with D/E compressing from 1.42x to 0.78x. Services at $30.98B with 76%+ margins and a 2.5B+ device installed base provide structural durability. However, valuation is not cheap: PE of 34.5x sits mid-range vs its 30-43x 365-day history, and the 2.9% earnings yield sits below the 4.41% 10Y Treasury, implying a negative equity risk premium. The stock is 1.6% below its 52-week high, meaning much of the fundamental improvement is already priced in. Near-term catalysts are meaningful: Q3 guidance of 14-17% revenue growth nearly doubled Street expectations of 9.5%, and the $100B buyback authorization plus dividend raise are unambiguously shareholder-friendly. The CEO transition to Ternus (with Cook as executive chairman) introduces modest uncertainty but appears orderly. Tariff headwind ($3.3B absorbed, accelerating to $1.4B/quarter) and oil at $98.38/bbl are real but manageable given $82.6B H1 operating cash flow. Net: strong business, full but not extreme valuation, credible near-term catalysts tilt mildly positive.
key_factors: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.18B (+16.6% YoY), EPS $2.01 (+21.8% YoY) — accelerating growth at massive scale
Gross margin expanded to 49.3% (vs 47.1% YoY), operating margin 32.3% — margin expansion across all levels
Operating cash flow $28.70B in Q2 (+19.8% YoY); H1 OCF $82.6B (+53% YoY) — cash-backed earnings
Balance sheet deleveraged: D/E from 1.42x to 0.78x, total equity $106.49B vs debt $82.70B
PE 34.5x mid-range vs 30-43x 365-day range; earnings yield 2.9% below 10Y Treasury 4.41% — negative equity risk premium
Q3 FY2026 guidance 14-17% revenue growth vs Street ~9.5% — nearly double consensus, strong forward catalyst
$100B new buyback authorization + 4% dividend raise + retirement of net-cash-neutral target — shareholder-friendly capital allocation
Services revenue $30.98B (76%+ gross margin), 2.5B+ installed base, 92% iPhone retention — structural moat
Tariff costs $3.3B absorbed since Apr 2025, accelerating to $1.4B/quarter; oil at $98.38/bbl is supply-chain cost headwind
CEO transition: Cook to executive chairman Sep 2026, John Ternus (25yr veteran) as CEO — orderly but introduces execution uncertainty

Apple has absorbed $3.3 billion in tariff costs since April 2025... quarterly expenses accelerating from $800 million to $1.4 billion
